question: How much detector compute can keyframing + target-ROI remove before S0 paddle quality degrades? (D-FINE is ~14.6s of the ~23s research path.)
method: detect_paddle.py extended with --roi (normalized crop, boxes mapped back to full-frame; D-FINE runs at a fixed input size so ROI is a QUALITY lever — measured ms/frame is ~constant — while STRIDE is the latency lever). Grid: {stride 1,2,3,4} x {full, target-ROI} on the two DEV cases' event-gated spans; target ROI = union of target torso positions + 2.6x torso-span reach margin from people.json. Scored S0-level vs gold visible paddle labels (hit = det center within 0.05 of label; labels without a detector frame within half the stride interval count as misses — keyframing pays for what it skips).
findings: STRIDE IS NEARLY FREE AT S0 on these cases: rally1 keeps 0.846-0.923 recall from stride 1→4 while inference drops 12.2s→2.9s (−76%).

TARGET ROI IMPROVES QUALITY where the player is small in frame (volley 0.25→0.375 at stride 1; 0.5 at stride 2-3) and is neutral when the target already fills the frame (rally1) — consistent with a fixed-input-size detector seeing the paddle at higher effective resolution.

ms/frame is ~constant (~90-120ms) across ROI settings — ROI does NOT reduce per-frame cost; candidate shortlist for the production point: STRIDE 3 + TARGET ROI (−65% detector compute, S0 recall ≥ stride-1 full-frame on both dev cases).
Volley stride-1 recall (0.25) below stride-2/3 is small-n label-timing noise (8 visible labels; nearest-frame reach criterion), not evidence that skipping frames improves detection.
caveats: S0-level only: tracking/ownership/contact/stroke NOT evaluated per cell — the stride-3+ROI operating point must run the FULL pipeline (cascade + benches) before promotion.
n = 21 visible labels on 2 dev cases; per-cell differences of one hit move recall by 0.08-0.12.
Static per-clip ROI; dynamic per-frame ROI with full-frame recovery unimplemented.
Wall-time includes fixed model-load overhead per run (~2-4s) that amortizes differently in production.
